title: Release v1.14.5
body:
An [announcement](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/Tx7unHaTwvo/m/5ZfJufnbAQAJ) from the Go team:

> We plan to issue Go 1.26.5 and Go 1.25.12 during US business hours on Tuesday, July 7.
> 
> These minor releases include PRIVATE security fixes to the standard library, covering the following CVE:
>
> -   CVE-2026-39822

The latest CoreDNS release 1.14.4 was built on Go 1.26.3 and is vulnerable to these three (fixed in 1.26.4):

- https://<redacted-host>/vuln/GO-2026-5037
- https://<redacted-host>/vuln/GO-2026-5038
- https://<redacted-host>/vuln/GO-2026-5039

I think we also have enough code changes for a new minor version release: https://github.com/coredns/coredns/compare/v1.14.4...master


I'm proposing we do a new release once Go 1.26.5 is out.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Also worth to take several security related fixes in before the release. Will take a scan as well.

comments.body:
Hmm,and looks like there's no fix for this in dd-trace-go: https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/issues/4984

I think we can just downgrade the dependency to `<2.9.0`. I can open a PR shortly.

Not sure we can rebuild with patch as the commit and version will be inconsistent. Maybe one way is to release another version 1.14.6 with the patch?
